en.title: Val Thorens powder forecast next week (23–29 November 2026): 30 cm up top
en.description: Next week's fresh snow in Val Thorens: 13–46 cm on the upper slopes and 11–39 cm at the base (23–29 November 2026), best day, best slopes and how sure the forecast is.
en.lede: Next week's snow numbers for Val Thorens: 30 cm at the top, 28 cm at mid-mountain, 25 cm at the base, all as the middle of a range for 23–29 November. The top's range runs from 13 to 46 cm, which says as much as the middle value does.

p: If you can pick one day, take the one that follows Wednesday 25 November, when 10 cm (up to 11 cm) has landed on the upper mountain.

Go high: depth is safest on the Péclet glacier and Cime Caron, and the best skiing should be on the Péclet side and the Cime Caron bowl, where shade keeps the snow dry. Treat the Orelle side, which faces the sun and the Maurienne valley as the weak point.

sections.h: How the week of 23–29 November adds up in Val Thorens
p: At the top (around 3100 m) the week totals 30 cm, 13–46 cm across our range. Mid-mountain around 2500 m gets 28 cm (12–43 cm), and the base around 1800 m 25 cm (11–39 cm).
The snow is not spread evenly. The days that matter at the top are Wednesday 25 (10 cm, up to 11), Thursday 26 (8 cm, up to 13) and Sunday 29 (6 cm, up to 12); the rest of the week is close to dry.

sections.h: This week in Val Thorens: the set-up
p: Before next week even starts, Val Thorens should be holding a deep fresh layer up high: 82 cm from Tuesday 17 to Friday 20 November (59–105 cm), while the base sees 42 cm. The second storm then builds on it.

sections.h: Snow or rain at the bottom?
p: The base gets nearly as much as the top (25 against 30 cm), which means the snow line stays below the lowest lifts for most of the week. Snow down to the village is the likely picture.
Val Thorens is the highest resort village of the Three Valleys, and it usually opens early because of that.
For comparison, the upper slopes of the closest big resorts collect Méribel (10 km away) 28 cm, Courchevel (14 km away) 27 cm and La Plagne (27 km away) 28 cm; Val Thorens sits at 30 cm.
Nothing to separate them on snow alone; the choice comes down to the terrain you want.
Reasonably, with a caveat. The snow is coming to Val Thorens, but the top could end up anywhere between 13 and 46 cm, and the middle value of 30 cm is only the halfway mark.
The days closest to now are the most reliable; the end of the week is the least.

advice: Fresh snow on a young snowpack: read the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif before any off-piste plan.
Opening dates are the resort's call; our numbers only say how much snow is coming.
Watch the forecast midweek: the top's range is 13–46 cm.
